points.text: LMM-score judge lacks human-agreement study, robustness check or alternative judge
GPT-5-mini judging GPT-5 raises self-preference and calibration concerns
Listed metric anomalies left unresolved
LMM-score scale uninterpretable; 'pixel-accurate' claims unsupported
Code-level vs visual-fidelity conclusion compares incommensurable, saturated scores
Treatment of non-executable outputs unclear; scores likely over different subsets
Level 3 compares only five proprietary models
Level 3 confounds chart generation with context-window and table processing; no ablation
Level 3 small (85 charts, 150 instructions); low statistical power
Pervasive numerical inconsistencies between tables, text and appendix
Several anomalous table entries unexplained
Inconsistent naming and unclear model count
No variance, seeds or confidence intervals despite fine-grained conclusions
Low open-source execution rates may reflect evaluation setup (V100, token limits, temperature)
'Thinking helps' claim rests on few model pairs without variance
Prompt sensitivity, dependency versions and sandbox failures not analysed
No failure taxonomy explaining why models fail
Novelty mainly bundles ChartMimic-style, ChartEdit-style and long-table tasks
Hierarchy of levels not validated; levels not comparable; tiny difficulty analysis
Level 2 reuses Level 1 charts, bounding diversity
L2 instruction filtering unclear; LLM-assisted ground truth correctness unquantified
No contamination analysis despite public chart sources and ChartMimic reuse
L1 figure-data and raw-data settings tiny (108, 36 items)
Dataset counting units and statistics confusing
Inter-rater agreement statistic unspecified
Typos, cut-off sentence, abstract numbers not matching tables
Saturation motivation uses GPT-4o scores not evaluated here
No qualitative model-level analysis; few insights
Incremental over ChartMimic: adds Level 3 and scale; insufficient for top venue
Near-identical phrasing, figures and design to ChartMimic
ChartMimic cited only in passing; potential plagiarism/integrity issue
Reuses ChartMimic data sources and evaluation protocols; minimal advancement
Overlap raises data ownership and double-submission concerns
Full dataset not released; limits reproducibility
GPT-5-mini judge may introduce bias; limited human validation
Surprising metric results (Seed, MiMo vs GPT-5) unexamined; LMM-score may not reflect correctness
Level 3 has only 150 tasks from 39 files
Level 3 tests long-context retrieval, not complex data wrangling
Only Matplotlib; no interactive or declarative libraries
No unified composite metric for model ranking
